sections.h2: Where is Richmond, Kentucky, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Richmond is the seat of Madison County, set in the Bluegrass region about 26 miles south of Lexington and 110 miles southeast of Louisville, according to the city's own site. Colonel John Miller founded it in 1798 and named it for his birthplace in Virginia, with incorporation following in 1809. The Kentucky River forms the county's northern edge, and the city spreads over roughly 19 to 20 square miles.

History matters to housing here. Confederate forces won the Battle of Richmond on August 30, 1862, and a normal school opened in 1906 that grew into Eastern Kentucky University. After rapid growth in the late 1990s and early 2000s, Richmond became the seventh largest city in Kentucky. The city also draws visitors to its many festivals, the Millstone Festival most of all.

sections.h2: What does the Census count for Richmond homes and renters?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts the city at 40,663 people for July 2025, up from a 2020 base of 35,164, spread over 15,202 households of about 2.17 people. Growth that quick keeps pressure on both rentals and starter homes.

With under four in ten households owning, most occupied Richmond housing is rented. A seller with tenants in place should be ready to hand over leases and rent records when a buyer asks.

sections.h2: What does Eastern Kentucky University mean for a Richmond house sale?
sections.html:
The university keeps Richmond young. In the 2020 count the median age stood at 29.1 years, and single person households made up 37.4 percent of the total. Housing built for students and young workers is a big part of what changes hands in town.

An owner who inherited a rental, or who is tired of managing one, has three paths: sell with tenants in place, wait for the lease to end, or close with a buyer who takes over the lease. Read the lease end date and the notice terms before you answer any offer.

sections.h2: Which city permit and code rules can complicate a Richmond sale?
sections.html:
Richmond's building inspection office (859-625-6428) enforces the 2018 Kentucky Building Code and related standards. If a prior owner finished a basement, added a deck or swapped a furnace without paperwork, the gap can surface during a buyer's inspection.

  • Permits are required for new construction, structural additions, basement remodels that change the occupant load, and room additions.
  • Sheds and garages need a permit once they reach 200 square feet in a residential setting.
  • Decks and porches need one at 200 square feet, at 30 inches above the ground, or when roofed or attached to the dwelling.
  • Furnace, air conditioner and electrical panel replacements need permits, and electrical and HVAC installers who are not the homeowner need a city business license.
  • Exterior work inside the H1 historic district goes before the Architectural Review Board, and ground mounted solar is not allowed in residential sections.
  • Permit work is inspected in stages, typically footer, foundation, slab, envelope, framing or rough-in, and a final, and the permit holder must call for each one.

If a seller built a deck or finished a room years ago, ask the office whether a permit was ever pulled and request a final sign-off on any open one. Applications can be filed through the city's online Accela portal or on paper at the office. Plumbing permits come from the state plumbing division or the local plumbing inspector rather than the city.

Codes Enforcement applies the property maintenance code published by the International Code Council and meets as a board on the second Wednesday of each month at 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, 239 W. Main Street. Call 859-625-6404 about an open case before you list.

sections.h2: What do Richmond's roads and schools look like to a buyer?
sections.html:
Interstate 75 runs along the west side with three exits, and U.S. 25 and 421 form the eastern bypass toward Lexington. State Route 876 loops around the business district. Berea is about 14 miles south on U.S. 25. The Blue Grass Army Depot lies southeast of the city, and CSX freight trains pass through town in both directions.

  • Madison County Schools serves the city, since the old Richmond district merged into it in 1988.
  • Elementary schools include Daniel Boone, Glenn Marshall, Kit Carson and White Hall, plus Madison Kindergarten Academy.
  • Middle schools are Madison Middle, B. Michael Caudill and Clark Moores, and Madison Central is the main high school.
  • Model Laboratory School is tied to the university.

Summers run hot and damp and winters stay mild to cool, which puts the age of the air conditioner high on an inspector's list.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax on a Richmond house?
sections.html:
Madison County's Sheriff collects the bill at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, with mail and online portal options as well. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30 and answers at 859-623-1511. Exemptions for homestead and disability go through the county PVA at 859-623-5410. The city's finance page adds that card and online payments are accepted for property taxes. A mortgage servicer may pay from escrow, yet the owner still receives a bill notice and should confirm that payment went out.

KRS 134.015 treats the tax as the debt of whoever held title on the January 1 assessment date. Paying everything on or before November 1 saves 2 percent, the plain amount is due until December 31, and the late charge is 5 percent in January and 10 percent once February arrives. The sheriff's office notes that buyers and sellers commonly prorate the year's tax at closing, with the current owner answerable for seeing that the bill gets paid.

sections.h2: Can a Richmond owner still contest a 2026 assessment?
sections.html:
For 2026 it is. KRS 133.045 opens the real property roll to public inspection for 13 days beginning in early May, with Saturday hours, and a taxpayer who wants to appeal must first ask the PVA for a conference. That period ended in May 2026, and the next one comes around each spring.

A seller can still use the conference to learn how the value was built. Bring recent neighborhood sales and ask the PVA to walk through the calculation. A value above what nearby houses fetch raises the bill that follows the house to its next owner.

sections.h2: What does a Richmond seller pay at closing?
sections.html: The seller bears Kentucky's deed transfer tax, set at $0.50 per $500 slice of the price, counting any partial slice (KRS 142.050). A deed at the city's typical $214,900 value owes $215.00, because 430 units of $500 are counted. Other items on the statement include the prorated property tax, payoff of any mortgage or lien, and an agent's commission if you list. A cash sale drops the commission and repair work from that list, so compare the final net rather than the headline price.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed to swap out a Richmond furnace?
faqs.a: Yes. Furnace and air conditioner change-outs are on the city's permit list, and the finished work gets inspected. Phone Building Inspections at 859-625-6428 before a contractor starts, because a missing permit tends to surface once a buyer orders an inspection.

faqs.q: Is Richmond mostly a renter city?
faqs.a: Yes. Census QuickFacts shows 38.3 percent of households owning, so about 62 percent rent.

faqs.q: Where does a Richmond owner send the county tax payment?
faqs.a: To the Madison County Sheriff at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, through the sheriff's online tax portal or by check. Never mail cash. Staff answer at 859-623-1511 on weekdays.

faqs.q: Can a Richmond house with code violations be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, though calling Codes Enforcement first at 859-625-6404 saves surprises. Its board meets on the second Wednesday of the month at 5:30 p.m., and knowing the status of an open case lets you describe it plainly to a buyer.

faqs.q: Which transfer tax applies to a Richmond sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays 50 cents on every $500 of price, counting partial blocks, so a $214,900 deed owes $215.00. Foreclosure deeds and some family transfers are exempt.
